summary: New Linux-scope runtime starts retain operation-owned producer closure evidence so revoked starts can retire behind a terminal PTY row without a PID, including a row from an older operation; legacy starts without this evidence remain held

replay.detail: No graph replay; reconciliation rechecks retained revoked starts.

schema.detail: No database schema change or registry row deletion. New Linux-scope launches persist versioned operation-owned launcher, publication and scope evidence in local runtime state.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No wire contract change. Non-terminal incarnation-less rows remain blocked and now record a diagnostic. Native Linux-scope closure requires acknowledged launchers and empty operation-owned work and server scopes; detached, crash-before-ack and legacy launches without ownership remain held.

manual.detail: Legacy unresolved launches without persisted operation ownership cannot be certified automatically. They remain held until an operator independently establishes physical producer and work-scope closure; a missing row, free lock or missing scope alone is not proof. Do not delete registry rows or edit the ledger as a substitute.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the previous conservative retention of terminal incarnation-less rows.
